name: Sandra Gómez
about:
I'm a multidisciplinary designer based in Barcelona, passionate about the intersection of art, technology, and human experience. I work across AI creative direction, immersive installations, interactive media, and photography — always searching for the emotional core of every project.

Currently pursuing a Master of Science in Digital Arts and Creative Technologies at La Salle Barcelona. Before that, years of hands-on work crafting campaigns, visual identities, and spatial experiences for brands and cultural projects.

I believe great design doesn't just look good — it makes people feel something.

tagline: Merging art, design & artificial intelligence to craft innovative visual experiences.
title: Multidisciplinary Designer

projects.approach:
I combined AI image generation with careful art direction to keep every render on-brand — matching Escribà's real product textures, packaging and studio lighting so the final images could sit next to traditional photography without looking out of place.

Each visual went through multiple generation and retouching passes, refining composition, color and detail until the output reached campaign-ready quality.
projects.title: Escribà — AI Creative Direction
projects.content: AI-generated high-end visual assets and brand imagery for Escribà's artisan pastry collections. Photorealistic 8K quality for global campaigns.

projects.approach:
I designed the spatial and interaction logic first, then layered visuals and sound on top so the room would react naturally to how people moved through it, rather than feeling like a fixed playback loop.

Testing happened directly in the space with real visitors, adjusting sensitivity and timing until the experience felt immediate and intuitive.

projects.content: Interactive multimedia experience designed and produced for an immersive spatial installation.

projects.approach:
Rather than building toward objectives or scores, I focused on mood and pacing — letting sound, visuals and touch guide the visitor through the piece at their own rhythm.

The result is closer to a short, contained journey than a game: something meant to be felt rather than won.
projects.title: Mini Interactive Experience
projects.content: A self-contained interactive experience — not a game, but an immersive journey through sound, visuals and touch.

projects.approach:
I followed the tour as it naturally unfolded, documenting the interaction between the visitors, the artworks and the studio itself. Rather than staging every moment, we focused on authentic reactions, movement and spontaneous details.

The photography explored the different areas of Studio 46—from its gallery rooms and original architectural features to its printing presses, tools and working spaces. The visual direction combined wider environmental shots with close-up details to communicate the studio’s intimate, lived-in character and its connection to generations of artists.
deliverables: Visual documentation of the studio’s creative process
projects.title: Studio 46
projects.content:
Studio 46 approached me to create a series of photographs that could capture the character of the space while visitors experienced a guided tour. Located in a historic family home in Barcelona’s Gràcia neighbourhood, the studio brings together architecture, printmaking, contemporary art and decades of artistic heritage.

The images were created for the studio’s website and digital communication, with the aim of presenting not only the artworks, but also the atmosphere, history and unique details visitors encounter throughout the space.
